✎From the Group Chat✎

Kaylani writes: Today's news you didn't ask for. In Rosenberg, Texas, a man reportedly drove his car through a locked Kroger pharmacy entrance after finding the store closed, because he needed to use the restroom. No injuries were reported. Some people knock. Some people find a gas station. This gentleman chose automotive demolition. Today's takeaway: when nature calls, please do not answer with your vehicle.

✶The Ledger✶

Colleges with no application fee
140
Governor Hochul says 140 New York colleges will waive application fees: all of SUNY, plus private colleges that just signed on. At any of those 140, the application itself now costs nothing.

✶The National Wire✶

1

Pope Leo Has Lung Cancer

Surgeons removed the lower lobe of the pope's right lung Tuesday in a roughly 90-minute operation, and tests confirmed lung cancer, the Vatican said. It called the surgery successful, with no complications, and said he had a peaceful night.

2

Judge Blocks White House Press Ban

A federal judge ruled late Tuesday that the White House can't shut out CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters over their coverage, at least until the case goes to trial. Judge Timothy Kelly said pulling their passes likely violated their First and Fifth Amendment rights.

3

Guilfoyle Out as Ambassador

The White House asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as ambassador to Greece on Tuesday, and she is stepping aside. Reports said she offered access to officials in exchange for help paying off her debt; she has denied the misconduct allegations.

4

40 Years for Tupac's Killing

Duane Davis, a former gang leader, was sentenced to 40 years for orchestrating the drive-by shooting that killed Tupac Shakur. A jury found him guilty last month; the rap star was shot in Las Vegas in 1996.

☑ The Ballot · 20 days to Election Day · early voting opens in 10 days, Oct 24, the same day registration closes · Hochul and Blakeman met last night in their first and only debate, sparring over Trump

⛪The Home Wire⛪

1

Rochester · Orangutans a Step Closer to Returning

Monroe County lawmakers voted 22–4 Tuesday night to advance a major expansion of the Seneca Park Zoo. It brings orangutans and lemurs one step closer to coming back.

2

North Tonawanda · A 4.25% Tax Increase Proposed

The city's proposed 2027 budget carries a 4.25 percent property tax increase. If it passes as written, city property tax bills go up again next year.

★The Marquee★

1

Girls Is Coming Back

Lena Dunham's HBO series returns for a limited run, ten years after its finale. HBO says the reunion takes on the milestone of turning forty.

2

Led Zeppelin Said Yes to Narnia

Robert Plant and Jimmy Page gave Greta Gerwig their blessing to use "Stairway to Heaven" in the first trailer for Narnia: The Magician's Nephew. The rock classic plays under the first look at the film.

3

Sorkin Misses The West Wing

Aaron Sorkin told Entertainment Weekly he thinks about reviving the NBC drama "a couple of seconds every day." "I miss it," he said of the series, which ran from 1999 to 2006.

⚑The Chase⚑

Phoenix Next
Sunday's race at Phoenix opens the last four. Kyle Larson holds the top spot, with Hamlin, Bell and Briscoe all within 65 points; the most points after Homestead on Nov. 8 takes the title. Daniel Suárez, 14th in the standings, will stay in Spire Motorsports' #7 Chevrolet next year under a contract extension.

☾On This Day☾

October 14, 1947 — Chuck Yeager flew the Bell X-1 faster than the speed of sound over California's Mojave Desert, the first pilot to do it. He had named the plane Glamorous Glennis, after his wife.
